clue.text: No mountain in south Africa is worthy of mention!

parts.note: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town in South Africa

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a lack of peaks in southern Africa is newsworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Table Mountain is the flat-topped landmark above Cape Town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable or noteworthy deserves to be talked about.

clue.text: Heads north having doled out last of supplies

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of doled are thrown into disorder
last of picks the final letter of the word supplies

explanation.surface: A leader goes north after rationing the last of the stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like a verb (leads north), but it is the plural noun; 'out' rearranges the letters of 'doled' into ODDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle is an informal word for the skull or head, so its plural matches.

clue.text: Dragged along to get married!

parts.note: to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A joke that being hauled to the altar is like being tugged behind a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that is towed is pulled behind another on a rope or bar.

clue.text: Commanding support for opening bowler on the boundary

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other
opening takes just the initial letter of the word bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket image of an order backing up the opening bowler near the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'support for' puts ORDERING below the B from 'opening bowler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordering means lying along the edge or frontier of something.

clue.text: 'Ummed and 'awed and got nicked

definitions.meaning: hummed and hawed means hedged; the dropped aitches mirror the dropped H, giving the word without its first letter
in cricket a batsman who gets a faint touch on the ball has nicked it

explanation.surface: Someone dithers in speech and then gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes show dropped aitches, so HEDGED loses its H. 'nicked' looks like British slang for arrested, but here it is the cricket sense of a thin touch off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who nicks the ball off the edge of the bat is said to have edged it; dithering is hedging.

clue.text: Cat and dog? Maybe just a dog

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cat and dog together make one pet, then settles for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, an old naval whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slender racing breed similar to a small greyhound.

clue.text: Saw that the west end is sinful

indicators.note: sinful suggests the letters of west end is have gone astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone observes that London's theatre district is a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and shopping district; 'sinful' rearranges WESTENDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To have witnessed something is to have seen it happen as an onlooker.

clue.text: Bonds that link clubs?

definitions.meaning: fetters or shackles that bind a prisoner
golf clubs of a certain type with metal heads

explanation.surface: A question about the ties that join social clubs together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like societies, but it is golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackles are made of metal, and a set of golf sticks includes numbered metal-headed ones.

clue.text: Crude part played by favourite — with hesitation

parts.note: a part played by an actor is a role
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Describes a rough performance by a star actor who keeps stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like an adjective about the acting, but it is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude is unrefined oil straight from the ground.

clue.text: Rulers like this sorely try the workers

indicators.note: sorely suggests the word try is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Bosses of this kind really test their staff's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' is a crossword staple for the insects of a colony; 'sorely' rearranges 'try' into TYR.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots are oppressive, absolute holders of power.

clue.text: Totally blue and Tory!

parts.note: Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: Describes someone completely Conservative, blue being the Tory colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative (Tory) party, which misleads; here it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means utterly or thoroughly.

clue.text: Animal often appearing in earthenware!

indicators.note: appearing in says the creature shows up inside the word for earthenware, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: earthenware is a kind of pottery

explanation.surface: A creature that is often depicted on clay pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the word for earthenware and lose its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquatic mammal of rivers, a classic crossword beast.

clue.text: Deposit required for gatekeeper's cottage

definitions.meaning: to deposit it, as a complaint or money
a small house at the gates of an estate

explanation.surface: A down payment is needed to rent the cottage at the estate gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To place formally, as with a complaint; also the porter's house by park gates.

clue.text: Adopt an informal approach to reprimand

explanation.surface: Being casual in manner as a way of telling someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear casual clothes; also to scold someone severely.

clue.text: Identifies condition found in animal group

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a species is a group of animals

explanation.surface: A zoologist names a disease discovered in a group of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' looks like an illness but is the word IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To name or state precisely, pinning something down.

clue.text: Discharges oriental delegations

explanation.surface: Eastern embassies are dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Releases of gas or fumes into the air.

clue.text: Troubles enveloping united Israel are fantasies

indicators.note: enveloping says the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is a name for Israel

explanation.surface: Unrest surrounding a unified Israel is wishful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: SION is a variant spelling of Zion, the Jewish homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Delusions or false impressions, things imagined.

clue.text: Sailor accepting soldiers' forebodings

indicators.note: accepting says the sailor takes the soldiers inside

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman taking in soldiers has premonitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents or signs of what is to come.

clue.text: Candid over the lack of restrictions?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the adjective, having no fixed limits

explanation.surface: Frank comments about there being no limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlimited in scope or duration, without fixed boundaries.

clue.text: Cast or bandage?

definitions.meaning: a support for an injured arm hung from the neck

explanation.surface: Asking whether a broken arm needs plaster or a wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a plaster cast, but it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something; also a cloth support for an injured arm.

clue.text: What's the weather like for some tennis — okay!

parts.note: a set is part of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Asking about conditions for a tennis match and hearing they're fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast term for settled, sunny conditions.

clue.text: A bigamist's meal in sad break up

indicators.note: break up suggests the letters of meal in sad are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man with two wives sees his miserable dinner fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'; 'break up' rearranges MEALINSAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser fond of female company, which a man with two wives might be called.

clue.text: What a composer does when sent to a school?

indicators.note: school, meaning to train, suggests the letters of sent to a are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what happens to a pupil sent off to boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb meaning to train or discipline, so it signals a rearrangement of SENTTOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes down music in notation on staves.

clue.text: Precedents set in cricket trials?

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Earlier rulings set during cricket matches.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international five-day cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal rulings that set a pattern for later judgments.

clue.text: Trace defective supply

indicators.note: defective suggests the word trace is faulty and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tracking down faulty provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide food or what is needed for an event.

clue.text: Nick's bargain?

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for to ...

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick has a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is the verb meaning pinch; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilfer; also something bought for very little.

clue.text: Head of prisons in true dilemma after break out

indicators.note: in places the prisons initial inside the rearranged letters
dilemma suggests the word true is in a muddle and rearranged
head of takes the opening letter of prisons

explanation.surface: A prison governor in a quandary after a jailbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilemma' turns TRUE into ERUT, and 'in' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or riot bursts forth suddenly.

clue.text: Custom in America, say, on the up?

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A habit in America that's growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means habitual practice or convention.

clue.text: Assume party is in suitable surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the first piece encloses the second

explanation.surface: Presuming the party is in a fitting venue.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a manner or name, as one takes up a stance.

clue.text: Finished the scheme in debt

parts.note: a draft is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: Completing the plan puts one in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank allowance to spend more than is in the account.

clue.text: Haunts full of soldier types?

explanation.surface: Places packed with military kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Places one frequently visits, such as holiday spots.

clue.text: Steps up runs

explanation.surface: Someone climbs and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' are ladders in British usage, a split in stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing frames with rungs; also British term for snags in tights.
